sections.title: Global Governance and Cooperation: International Education Policy and Practice
sections.description: This course examines global governance in education from a policy perspective. Drawing on diverse disciplinary approaches – including international relations, economics, anthropology/sociology, and development studies –students will explore the key actors involved in international educational policy making; how policy is created, financed, and evaluated; and how these actors and policies impact various fields of education (e.g. early childhood education, higher education, EdTech, etc.). The course aims to help students develop the skills needed to critically engage with and design global educational policy in an increasingly globalized yet bordered world. By the end of the course, students will have deepened their understanding of the history, current iterations, and future directions of global governance and international cooperation in education and have acquired the analytical skills necessary to contribute to the global education policy field. The course is open to all graduate students interested in international development, public policy, and global education.

sections.title: Global Governance and Cooperation: International Education Policy and Practice
sections.description: This course focuses on the intersection of global education policy and international development. Drawing on diverse disciplinary perspectives – including policy sciences, international relations, and development studies – students will explore the role of global governance institutions and international development policy in facilitating or constraining progress toward the Sustainable Development Goals. Through course assignments and in-class discussions with development practitioners, students will examine how actors and institutions influence the global governance of education and its implementation in low- and middle-income countries. By the end of the course, students will have deepened their understanding of the history, current status, and future directions of international cooperation in education and acquired analytical skills to contribute to the global education policy field. The course is open to all graduate students with interests in global education, public policy, and international development. The format includes mandatory synchronous sessions twice a week along with weekly asynchronous assignments.
